title: Cryopreservable dopaminergic progenitors derived from human iPSCs with accelerated loss of pluripotency and early functional restoration in Parkinsonian rats.
cell_types: PBMC-derived iPSC midbrain dopaminergic progenitor spheroids
study_design: Differentiation, spheroid storage/recovery and transplantation workflow; cryopreservation feasibility with delayed phenotype and rat behavioral outcomes
interventions: STEM-CELLBANKER plus ROCK inhibitor and RevitaCell
n-butylidenephthalide during differentiation (not a demonstrated CPA)

experiments.model: Healthy-donor PBMC-derived iPSC midbrain dopaminergic progenitor spheroids
experiments.cooling: Isopropanol Cryo 1 °C container precooled to 4 °C; −80 °C for 24 h then liquid nitrogen; measured rate not reported
experiments.warming: 37 °C bath until small ice remains; dilute with DMEM/F12, centrifuge and resuspend
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen, 3 months; marker comparison also tested 11 months
experiments.intervention: Freeze day-23 reaggregated dopaminergic progenitor spheroids using the combined commercial medium/recovery workflow
experiments.comparator: Prefreeze cell counts and 3-versus-11-month storage comparison
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw viable-cell recovery and dopaminergic identity
experiments.timepoint: Immediate thaw; phenotype 22 days after thaw
experiments.result: After 3-month storage, reported survival was 85.48 ± 5.16% and recovery (post/pre cell-number ratio) was 83.96 ± 9.96%. Viable cells per spheroid averaged 6.16 × 10^4 before and 5.24 × 10^4 after freezing. At 22 days after thaw, 71.04 ± 1.98% expressed TH/FOXA2; marker fractions did not significantly differ between 3- and 11-month storage. Do not derive the mean recovery by dividing the two grand means.
experiments.sample_size: Figure 5 n=8 independent experiments for immediate counts/viability/recovery; n=3 for marker comparison; not eight donors
experiments.source_locator: Results Cryopreservation of mDAp; Figure 5B–G; Methods mDAp cryopreservation and thawing
experiments.evidence_excerpt: the spheroids were thawed and exhibited healthy morphology

experiments.model: Healthy-donor PBMC-derived iPSC midbrain dopaminergic progenitor spheroids
experiments.cooling: Isopropanol Cryo 1 °C container precooled to 4 °C; −80 °C for 24 h then liquid nitrogen; measured rate not reported
experiments.warming: 37 °C bath until small ice remains; dilute with DMEM/F12, centrifuge and resuspend
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen, 3 months; marker comparison also tested 11 months
experiments.intervention: Transplant thawed progenitor spheroids prepared with the optimized differentiation workflow, including n-BP pretreatment
experiments.comparator: Medium control and additional cells differentiated without n-BP; no matched fresh-versus-frozen transplant comparison established here
experiments.outcome_name: Post-transplant motor behavior and graft maturation
experiments.timepoint: Functional recovery by 8 weeks; graft observation to 20 weeks and rotation follow-up to 24 weeks
experiments.result: Thawed grafts survived, formed TH-positive neurites and were associated with motor improvement in 6-OHDA Parkinsonian rats by eight weeks. A no-n-BP differentiation arm improved later. This is evidence of usability after storage, not a test that n-BP is an ice inhibitor or directly improves freeze-thaw survival.
experiments.sample_size: Figure 7 rotation groups n=8/13 rats and cylinder groups n=14/12; donor-independent replication not established
experiments.source_locator: Results graft maturation/motor recovery; Figure 7 and supplemental Figure S8 discussion; Methods transplantation
experiments.evidence_excerpt: accelerated motor recovery in Parkinsonian rats

main_finding: The combined workflow permits long-term spheroid storage followed by dopaminergic identity and animal functional outcomes, without isolating CPA ingredients or proving a dual-action cryoprotective molecule.
limitations: Main storage workflow uses one PBMC-derived line; H9 and IMR-90 differentiation checks do not establish matched multi-line cryopreservation validation.
Methods describe approximately 200 µm spheroids whereas results describe approximately 300 µm; diameter must be clarified before process transfer.
Methods use approximately 40 spheroids per 1 mL cryotube; ROCK-inhibitor identity/dose in the freezing mixture and commercial formulation composition are not specified in that section.
All components, differentiation and recovery handling vary together; no physical ice assay or ingredient-isolating freezing comparison is established.
Recovery and survival have distinct denominators; raw cell counts and paired sample IDs were not independently obtained.
The paper states raw imaging exceeds 1 TB and is available upon author request. No bulk download or outreach was performed.
n-BP differentiation effects and animal behavior do not establish cryoprotectant target engagement, clinical efficacy or a new CPA.
mechanism_claim: Direct evidence is storage/recovery, differentiation markers and animal graft function. n-BP is a differentiation intervention; no direct ice activity or isolated cryoinjury pathway effect is established.
reviewer: root selected methods, Figure 5/7 results and data-availability review
